steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO1 assesses: technical control (accuracy, fluency, intonation), expression (dynamics, phrasing, articulation), and interpretation (stylistic understanding, communication).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Choose a piece that shows your STRENGTHS — difficulty alone does not guarantee marks if you cannot perform it accurately and expressively.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Practice strategies: slow practice, sectional rehearsal, recording and self-evaluation, gradual tempo increase, focused work on difficult passages.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Minimum duration is 1 minute per piece — but quality matters more than length. A well-performed shorter piece can score higher than a poorly performed long one.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how solo performance are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use solo performance. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use solo performance in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how solo performance are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language. | A practical application showing understanding of how solo performance can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
